overall_summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum are extending their declines today as spot ETFs recorded 231 million dollars in outflows. A strategy authorizing up to 1.25 billion dollars in Bitcoin monetization is adding further bearish pressure. Broader markets are steady ahead of key economic data releases.

items.title: Bitcoin Spot ETFs See $231M Outflow on June 29
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net outflow of 231 million dollars yesterday according to CoinGlass data, extending a streak of redemptions. This comes as Bitcoin trades near 59 to 60 thousand dollars amid broader market caution. Traders should watch because sustained ETF selling can amplify downside pressure and signal weakening institutional demand. Sources include CoinGlass ETF tracker and Farside Investors flow data.
items.impact: Adds selling pressure and reinforces near-term caution on Bitcoin price.

items.title: Strategy Authorizes Up to $1.25B Bitcoin Monetization
items.summary: MicroStrategy rebranded as Strategy announced a new BTC monetization program on June 29 allowing sales of up to 1.25 billion dollars in Bitcoin. Proceeds target building a USD reserve, funding dividends and interest, or supporting buybacks. The move gives the company flexibility to treat its large Bitcoin holdings more dynamically. Traders should care because any actual sales could add supply to the market and weigh on price. Sources include Strategy press release and CoinDesk coverage.
items.impact: Potential future supply from corporate treasury could cap upside or trigger volatility.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum Extend Declines Amid ETF Outflows
items.summary: Bitcoin fell toward 59 thousand dollars and Ethereum traded near 1,570 dollars on June 29 as ETF outflows and shifting investor flows to AI-related assets persisted. Macro concerns around rates also weighed on risk assets. Traders should monitor because continued weakness in spot demand and flows keeps the path of least resistance lower in the short term. Sources include CoinDesk daybook and market recap reports.
items.impact: Reinforces downside momentum and tests key support levels for major cryptos.

items.title: Trump Signs Executive Orders on Quantum and Crypto Security
items.summary: President Trump signed executive orders on June 29 focused on advancing quantum computing and migrating to post-quantum cryptography for national security. The moves aim to protect data against future quantum threats but do not directly address digital assets or Bitcoin policy. Traders should note the limited immediate crypto market implications beyond broader tech sector sentiment. Sources include White House announcements.
items.impact: Minimal direct price impact but signals ongoing government focus on emerging tech security.

items.title: JOLTS Job Openings for May Due Today at 10 AM ET
items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases its May JOLTS report showing job openings, hires, and separations. Traders watch this closely as a gauge of labor market strength ahead of Friday's full employment report. Stronger than expected openings could signal resilience that keeps the Fed cautious on rate cuts, while weakness might ease those concerns and support risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Mixed impact on yields and equities depending on beat or miss.

items.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence for June Released
items.summary: The Conference Board releases its June consumer confidence index at 10 AM ET, alongside job openings data. This measures household sentiment on the economy and jobs, which can influence spending and growth outlooks. A surprise move higher or lower could shift views on consumer resilience and Fed policy path.
items.impact: Potential short-term moves in equities and yields on the print.

items.title: S&P Case-Shiller Home Price Index for April Out Today
items.summary: S&P releases its Case-Shiller 20-city home price index for April at 9 AM ET, along with FHFA house price data. Housing prices remain a key inflation component that the Fed monitors. Updates here can reinforce or ease views on persistent shelter inflation and rate cut timing.
items.impact: Minor influence on inflation expectations and bond yields.

items.title: Chicago PMI and Redbook Retail Data Scheduled
items.summary: Chicago Business Barometer PMI for June and Redbook retail sales YoY are due today. These provide early reads on manufacturing and consumer spending trends. Deviations from forecasts could add to the day's data flow and nudge short-term market sentiment.
items.impact: Limited but additive to daily macro volatility.

items.title: US Treasury Yields Little Changed Ahead of Data
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield hovers near 4.38 percent with minimal movement in the last session as markets await today's releases and Friday's jobs report. Yields remain elevated post-recent labor data and geopolitical factors. Stable yields keep the dollar supported and limit downside pressure on Bitcoin for now.
items.impact: Supports range-bound trading in risk assets.

items.title: DXY Holds Steady Near 101.6 Level
items.summary: The US dollar index remains around 101.6 amid quiet trading ahead of key US data releases. Broader strength from resilient labor markets and higher-for-longer rate expectations continues to underpin it. A firm dollar can weigh on Bitcoin and other risk assets by increasing opportunity costs for non-yielding holdings.
items.impact: Mild headwind for crypto and commodities if dollar strengthens further.

items.title: US, Iran Agree to Halt Attacks, Plan Doha Talks
items.summary: The US and Iran have agreed to stop recent strikes after weekend exchanges tested a fragile ceasefire, with delegations heading to Doha on Tuesday for talks on the Strait of Hormuz and broader issues. Oil prices rose initially on the flare-up but are now reacting to the pause. Traders should watch energy flows and any sanctions relief signals, as renewed tensions could spike crude and hit risk assets.
items.impact: Eases immediate oil supply fears but keeps markets on edge

items.title: Venezuela Quake Death Toll Tops 1,700
items.summary: Back-to-back powerful earthquakes on June 24 have killed more than 1,700 people in Venezuela, with the toll still rising amid ongoing rescues and aftershocks. International aid is arriving but challenges persist in the crisis-hit country. This humanitarian disaster could add volatility to regional markets and commodities.
items.impact: Limited direct market move but signals broader instability risks

items.title: Pakistan Strikes Afghanistan, Dozens Reported Dead
items.summary: Pakistan launched airstrikes and a ground operation in eastern Afghanistan, claiming to kill dozens of militants in response to recent attacks inside Pakistan. Afghan officials say at least 36 civilians died and over 160 were wounded. The escalation risks wider regional instability and could pressure energy routes and risk sentiment.
items.impact: Heightens cross-border tensions and potential supply disruptions
